:::{#thm-dot-linear-sum}
#### The dot product of a vector with a linear combination

For vectors $\vecf{x}, \vecf{u}_1, \ldots, \vecf{u}_k \in \reals^p$
and numbers $c_1, \ldots, c_k$,

$$
\vecf{x} \cdot \paren{\sum_{j=1}^{k} c_j \vecf{u}_j}
= \sum_{j=1}^{k} c_j\,(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{u}_j).
$$

:::

::: proof

Write $u_{ji}$ for entry $i$ of $\vecf{u}_j$. Then

$$
\ba
\vecf{x} \cdot \paren{\sum_{j=1}^{k} c_j \vecf{u}_j}
&= \sum_{i=1}^{p} x_i \sum_{j=1}^{k} c_j u_{ji}
&& \text{(@def-dot-product; entry } i \text{ of the combination)}
\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^{p} \sum_{j=1}^{k} x_i c_j u_{ji}
&& \text{(distribute each } x_i \text{ over the inner sum)}
\\
&= \sum_{j=1}^{k} \sum_{i=1}^{p} x_i c_j u_{ji}
&& \text{(swap the order of the finite sums)}
\\
&= \sum_{j=1}^{k} c_j \sum_{i=1}^{p} x_i u_{ji}
&& \text{(commute, then factor } c_j \text{ out of the inner sum)}
\\
&= \sum_{j=1}^{k} c_j\,(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{u}_j).
&& \text{(@def-dot-product)}
\ea
$$

For $k = 0$ both sides are $0$, since the empty combination is $\vzero$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-dot-linear-sum}
#### Dotting with a combination of three vectors

Let $\vecf{x} = (1, 2, 3)$ and take the combination
$2\,(1, 0, 0) - (0, 1, 0) + 4\,(0, 0, 1) = (2, -1, 4)$.
Directly, $\vecf{x} \cdot (2, -1, 4) = 2 - 2 + 12 = 12$.
By @thm-dot-linear-sum,
$2 \cd 1 - 1 \cd 2 + 4 \cd 3 = 12$, the same number.

:::
